CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 42-year-old female who sustained a right index finger injury while skiing on double black diamond slopes this past Saturday (5 days ago). She lost control, flipped down the slope, and jammed her right index finger on an unknown object. She denies other injuries from the fall. Pain is rated 7/10. She has taken ibuprofen without significant relief. She has not iced or splinted the finger. X-ray of the right hand shows normal alignment with no fractures.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation.
Appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger examination reveals tenderness to palpation over the distal interphalangeal joint with pain on pushing, pulling, and squeezing. X-ray of right hand is normal with no fractures or joint malalignment.

RESULTS
Right hand x-ray: normal, no fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right index finger. Plan includes application of finger splint, prescription of mobic 15 mg once daily (14 tablets), and follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine if hand therapy is needed.
